detail.longDescription: Gitflow strategy: main: Stores official, production-ready releases. develop: Serves as the integration branch for upcoming features. feature/*: Branches off develop for new features; merges back into develop. release/*: Branches off develop to prep a release (bug fixes/metadata); merges into both main and develop. hotfix/*: Branches off main for urgent production bugs; merges into both main and develop. We have rulesets that enforce pull requests to develop and main. The confusion arises when hotfix or release branch is merged with develop. I don't know how it happens, but sometimes the PR would show commits that already exist in the develop branch. Note that I do not squash-merge or rebase. Also note that I am talking about commits that have the exact same commit hash as the one on develop. I am not talking about merge commits. I searched far and wide and found no one talking about this issue. AI said it is caused by "crisscross merges" and its solution is as follows: Merge hotfix with main only. Make a new branch from develop. Merge master into that branch. Make a PR from that branch into develop. A new branch is created for making the PR, instead of making a PR directly from master, because our rulesets prevent direct pushes to master branch, so any conflicts in the master to develop PR cannot be resolved. Do you know a better solution?
